name: Brisk walking
form_cues: Walk tall with your eyes ahead, not at your feet.
Swing your arms naturally from the shoulders.
Pick a pace where you can talk but not sing.
common_mistakes: Strolling too slowly to raise your heart rate
Overstriding and landing hard on the heel
safety: Wear supportive shoes and start with shorter walks if you're new to exercise.
notes: Great daily base for fat loss and recovery days. Count your walk to the gym here.

name: Jogging
form_cues: Keep an easy, conversational pace.
Land lightly with your foot under your hips.
Relax your shoulders and keep your hands loose.
common_mistakes: Starting too fast and fading early
Long, heavy heel-striking strides
safety: Build weekly distance gradually (about 10% a week) to avoid shin and knee niggles.
notes: Couch-to-5K beginners can alternate 1 min jog / 2 min walk.

name: Run-walk intervals
form_cues: Jog for a set time, then walk briskly to recover.
Keep the jog easy enough to repeat every round.
Walk with purpose; don't stop completely.
common_mistakes: Running the jog bits too hard
Cutting walk breaks short before you've recovered
safety: Ease off if you feel sharp pain in shins, knees or feet.
notes: Classic start: 1 min jog / 1–2 min walk, repeated 8–10 times. Lengthen the jog each week.

name: Running
form_cues: Stand tall with a slight forward lean from the ankles.
Take quick, light steps landing under your hips.
Drive your elbows back and keep your hands relaxed.
common_mistakes: Overstriding and braking with each step
Tensing the shoulders and clenching fists
Running every run hard
safety: Increase distance slowly and replace worn-out shoes to protect knees and shins.
notes: Log distance and time; the app can work out your pace.

name: Tempo run
form_cues: Warm up with 10 minutes of easy jogging first.
Hold a pace you could keep for about an hour—comfortably hard.
Breathe rhythmically and stay relaxed.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a race
Skipping the warm-up and cool-down
safety: Only do tempo work once or twice a week, with easy days in between.
notes: You should be able to speak a few words, not full sentences.

name: Fartlek run
form_cues: Mix fast bursts with easy running, no fixed plan needed.
Pick landmarks: surge to the next lamppost, then recover.
Keep the easy bits genuinely easy.
common_mistakes: Making every surge an all-out sprint
Stopping to walk instead of jogging the recovery
safety: Warm up well before surges to protect your hamstrings and calves.
notes: Swedish for 'speed play'. A fun way to add speed without a track.

name: Interval repeats (400 m)
form_cues: Run each repeat at a hard but even pace.
Jog or walk 200 m (or 90 sec) between repeats.
Aim to run the last repeat as fast as the first.
common_mistakes: Blasting the first repeat and dying on the rest
Too little recovery between repeats
safety: Warm up for 10–15 minutes first; skip if you have a calf or hamstring strain.
notes: Log each repeat as a set. Works on a track, road or treadmill.

name: Sprint intervals
form_cues: Drive your knees up and arms hard, elbows at 90°.
Stay on the balls of your feet.
Walk back slowly to recover fully before the next one.
common_mistakes: Sprinting without a proper warm-up
Leaning back and reaching with the feet
Resting too little so quality drops
safety: Warm up thoroughly with jogging and drills; hamstring pulls are common with cold sprints.
notes: Typical session: 6–10 × 15–30 sec all-out, 1–2 min walk recovery.

name: Hill sprints
form_cues: Lean slightly into the hill from your ankles.
Take short, powerful steps and pump your arms.
Walk back down slowly as your recovery.
common_mistakes: Running back down fast and pounding the knees
Looking at your feet instead of up the hill
safety: Choose a moderate grade (5–10%) and a non-slippery surface.
notes: Sprint 10–20 sec up; count each climb as one rep. Easier on the hamstrings than flat sprints.

name: Stair runs
form_cues: Run up every step, landing on the balls of your feet.
Pump your arms and keep your chest up.
Walk down carefully, holding the rail if needed.
common_mistakes: Rushing the way down
Hunching over and looking at your feet
safety: Use dry, well-lit stairs and always walk—never run—back down.
notes: Take every second step for a glute-focused version.

name: High knees
aliases: Running in place with high knees
form_cues: Drive each knee up to hip height.
Stay light on the balls of your feet.
Pump your arms in time with your legs.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to lift the knees
Landing heavy on the heels
safety: Use a softer surface or march instead if you have knee or ankle pain.

name: Butt kicks
form_cues: Flick your heels up toward your glutes.
Keep your knees pointing down at the floor.
Stay quick and light on your toes.
common_mistakes: Knees swinging forward
Leaning the torso forward
safety: Stop if you feel a cramp or pull in the hamstring.

name: March in place
form_cues: Lift each knee to a comfortable height.
Swing your opposite arm with each step.
Stand tall and breathe steadily.
common_mistakes: Slouching forward
Shuffling with tiny lifts
safety: Hold a counter or wall for balance if you're unsteady.
notes: Zero-impact option for beginners, older adults or small spaces.

name: Jumping jacks
form_cues: Jump feet wide as your arms sweep overhead.
Land softly with knees slightly bent.
Keep a steady rhythm and breathe.
common_mistakes: Landing stiff-legged
Half-reaching with the arms
safety: Step side to side instead of jumping if you have knee, ankle or pelvic floor issues.

name: Step jacks
form_cues: Step one foot out to the side as arms rise overhead.
Bring the foot back in and lower the arms.
Alternate sides at a brisk tempo.
common_mistakes: Moving too slowly to raise the heart rate
Shrugging the shoulders
safety: Fine for most joint issues since there's no jumping.

name: Plank jacks
form_cues: Hold a straight plank on your hands.
Hop your feet wide, then back together.
Keep hips level and don't bounce them.
common_mistakes: Hips piking up
Sagging lower back
safety: Step feet out one at a time if your wrists or shoulders complain.

name: Squat thrusts
form_cues: Squat down and plant your hands outside your feet.
Jump both feet back into a plank, then back in.
Stand up tall to finish each rep.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging in the plank
Rounding the back when you squat
safety: Step back instead of jumping to protect wrists and lower back.

name: Step-back burpee
form_cues: Squat and place your hands on the floor.
Step one foot back, then the other, into a plank.
Step back in and stand up tall.
common_mistakes: Rushing and letting the hips sag
Not standing all the way up
safety: Put your hands on a bench or step to shorten the range if needed.

name: Burpees
form_cues: Squat, hands down, jump feet back to a plank.
Jump feet back in, then jump up with arms overhead.
Land softly and flow into the next rep.
common_mistakes: Belly flopping with a saggy back
Landing stiff-legged from the jump
safety: Scale to stepping if you have wrist, shoulder or low-back pain.

name: Push-up burpee
form_cues: Jump back to a plank and do a full push-up.
Keep your body in a straight line on the push-up.
Jump feet in, stand, and jump with a clap overhead.
common_mistakes: Worming up from the floor hips-first
Skipping the push-up range
safety: Drop the push-up when form slips; protect your shoulders and lower back.

name: Burpee broad jump
form_cues: Do a burpee, then jump forward as far as you can.
Swing your arms and land softly on both feet.
Go straight into the next burpee where you land.
common_mistakes: Landing with knees caving in
Rushing so the burpee gets sloppy
safety: Needs clear space ahead and a non-slip surface.
notes: Popular in CrossFit and HYROX training; can also be logged by distance.

name: Sprawls
form_cues: From a fighting stance, drop hands to the floor.
Shoot your legs back and drive hips down to the mat.
Snap your feet back under you and return to stance.
common_mistakes: Landing on straight arms and jarring the elbows
Hips staying high instead of pressing down
safety: Use a mat; build speed only once the movement is smooth.
notes: Takedown defence from wrestling/MMA and a brutal conditioning drill.

name: Mountain climbers
form_cues: Hold a strong plank, hands under shoulders.
Drive one knee to your chest, then switch quickly.
Keep your hips low and level.
common_mistakes: Hips bouncing up high
Shoulders drifting behind the hands
safety: Put hands on a bench or step to ease wrist and shoulder load.
notes: Can also be counted as reps (each knee drive = 1).

name: Cross-body mountain climbers
form_cues: Start in a high plank.
Drive each knee toward the opposite elbow.
Keep your shoulders over your hands throughout.
common_mistakes: Twisting the hips up high
Moving so fast the knee barely moves
safety: Slow down if your lower back starts to arch.

name: Bear crawl
form_cues: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, knees hovering just off the floor.
Move opposite hand and foot together.
Keep your back flat like a tabletop.
common_mistakes: Hips shooting up high
Big, sloppy steps
safety: Use a clear, non-slip floor and stop if wrists hurt.
notes: Crawl forward and backward, or log distance (e.g. 4 × 10 m) in notes.

name: Lateral shuffle
form_cues: Sink into a half squat with your chest up.
Push off the trailing foot and slide sideways.
Don't let your feet click together.
common_mistakes: Standing up tall between steps
Crossing the feet
safety: Wear shoes with lateral support; avoid slippery floors.

name: Shadowboxing
form_cues: Stay in stance with hands up guarding your chin.
Throw crisp punches and snap them back.
Keep moving your feet between combinations.
common_mistakes: Dropping the hands after punching
Fully locking the elbows on every punch
Standing flat-footed
safety: Don't snap your elbows straight; keep a tiny bend at full extension.
notes: Rounds are usually 3 min work / 1 min rest. Light hand weights are optional but go easy.

name: Shadow kickboxing
form_cues: Mix punches with kicks and knees, hands always up.
Turn your hips over on every kick.
Return to stance after each combination.
common_mistakes: Leaning way back on kicks
Dropping the guard while kicking
safety: Kick only as high as your hips allow; warm up the hips first.

name: Speed punches
form_cues: Square up with a slight bend in the knees.
Punch straight ahead, alternating as fast as you can.
Keep your core tight and shoulders down.
common_mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders up
Locking the elbows hard
safety: Keep a soft bend in the elbows to protect the joints.
notes: Common finisher in cardio kickboxing classes; works well as 20–30 sec intervals.

name: Front kick
form_cues: Lift the knee high, then push through the ball of the foot.
Lean back only slightly and keep your guard up.
Retract the leg quickly back to stance.
common_mistakes: Snapping the knee straight
Letting the hands drop
safety: Don't lock out the knee hard on air kicks.

name: Roundhouse kick
form_cues: Pivot on the ball of your standing foot.
Swing the hip through and strike with the shin.
Bring the leg back to stance with your hands up.
common_mistakes: Not pivoting the standing foot
Kicking with just the leg, no hip turn
safety: Warm up hips and hamstrings first; kick low until mobility allows higher.

name: Knee strikes
form_cues: Reach your hands forward as if gripping a head.
Drive the knee up and forward, hips through.
Rise onto the toes of the standing foot.
common_mistakes: Leaning back away from the knee
Lifting the knee without driving the hips
safety: Keep the standing knee soft; alternate legs to balance the load.

name: Trail running
form_cues: Shorten your stride on uneven ground.
Look 2–3 metres ahead, not at your feet.
Power-hike steep climbs; it's often just as fast.
common_mistakes: Overstriding downhill
Chasing road pace on rough terrain
safety: Tell someone your route, carry water, and watch for roots and rocks.

name: Hiking
form_cues: Take shorter steps going uphill.
Lean slightly forward on climbs and use your glutes.
Go slow and controlled on descents.
common_mistakes: Locking the knees on descents
Starting too fast up the first climb
safety: Check weather, carry water, and use poles if your knees struggle downhill.
notes: Log elevation gain in notes if your watch tracks it.

name: Freestyle swimming
form_cues: Keep your head down and body long and flat.
Rotate your body and reach long with each stroke.
Breathe to the side every 2–3 strokes.
common_mistakes: Lifting the head to breathe so the legs sink
Kicking from the knees instead of the hips
Crossing hands over the midline
safety: Swim in supervised areas; avoid open water alone.
notes: No app gear id exists for a pool, so 'req' is left empty—needs pool access.

name: Breaststroke
form_cues: Pull, breathe, kick, glide—in that order.
Snap your heels round in a whip kick.
Glide with arms extended before the next stroke.
common_mistakes: Skipping the glide
Keeping the head up the whole time
safety: Breaststroke kick can strain the inner knee; ease in if you have knee issues.
notes: Needs pool access; no app gear id for a pool.

name: Backstroke
form_cues: Lie flat with your ears in the water, eyes up.
Enter little-finger first, arms straight overhead.
Kick steadily from the hips with loose ankles.
common_mistakes: Sitting in the water with hips low
Bending the knees too much on the kick
safety: Count strokes from the flags so you don't hit the wall.
notes: Good for posture: opens the chest. Needs pool access.

name: Butterfly
form_cues: Move in a wave from chest to hips to feet.
Sweep both arms together, out of the water and forward.
Use two dolphin kicks per arm stroke.
common_mistakes: Lifting the head too high to breathe
Bending the knees for a big kick instead of a body wave
safety: Very demanding on the shoulders and lower back—build up slowly.
notes: Needs pool access.

name: Outdoor cycling
form_cues: Set saddle height so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom.
Spin smoothly; shift gears to keep your cadence up.
Relax your grip and keep elbows soft.
common_mistakes: Grinding a big gear at low cadence
Saddle too low causing knee pain
safety: Always wear a helmet and use lights in low visibility.
notes: No outdoor-bike gear id exists, so 'bike' (stationary bike) is used as the nearest match. Counts commuting too.

name: Rucking
form_cues: Wear the pack high and tight on your back.
Walk tall; don't lean far forward.
Keep a brisk, steady pace.
common_mistakes: Starting with a pack that's too heavy
Loose straps letting the load bounce
safety: Start around 10% of body weight and add load slowly to protect your back and feet.
notes: A loaded backpack works fine; 'weightvest' is the nearest app gear id.

name: Jump rope
form_cues: Turn the rope with your wrists, elbows close to your sides.
Jump just high enough to clear the rope.
Land softly on the balls of your feet.
common_mistakes: Jumping too high
Swinging the rope from the shoulders
Landing flat-footed
safety: Use a rope sized to your height and jump on a forgiving surface, not concrete.
notes: Can also be logged as reps (skips).

name: Boxer skip
form_cues: Shift your weight side to side, one foot lightly tapping.
Keep the bounce tiny and rhythmic.
Stay relaxed so you can go for full rounds.
common_mistakes: Landing on both feet evenly so it's just a basic bounce
Tense shoulders
safety: Ease in if your calves or Achilles are tight.
notes: Boxers' staple: lets you skip for 3-min rounds with less fatigue.

name: Alternate-foot jump rope
form_cues: Jog in place, one foot per rope turn.
Keep the knees low and the steps light.
Turn the rope from the wrists.
common_mistakes: Lifting the knees too high and catching the rope
Rushing the rope speed
safety: Wear supportive shoes and build up time gradually.

name: High-knee jump rope
form_cues: Drive each knee up to hip height as the rope passes.
Turn the rope fast to keep up with your feet.
Stay tall and land on the balls of your feet.
common_mistakes: Leaning back
Slowing the rope so the knees can't lift
safety: Stop if your hip flexors or calves feel strained.

name: Side-to-side jump rope
form_cues: Jump a few centimetres side to side with feet together.
Keep your shoulders square to the front.
Stay light and quick.
common_mistakes: Jumping too wide
Rolling the ankles on landing
safety: Avoid if you have unstable ankles.

name: Criss-cross jump rope
form_cues: Cross your arms at the waist on every second turn.
Push your hands past your hips when crossed.
Jump slightly higher on the crossing turn.
common_mistakes: Crossing the arms too high at the chest
Hands not wide enough so the loop is too small
safety: Use a slightly longer rope while learning.

name: Single-leg jump rope
form_cues: Hop on one foot with the other knee lifted slightly.
Keep the hops small and springy.
Hold your hips level.
common_mistakes: Hips dropping to one side
Landing heavy on the heel
safety: Build up slowly to avoid overloading the Achilles.

name: Double unders
form_cues: Jump a little higher with straight, tight legs.
Flick the wrists hard so the rope passes twice.
Keep elbows in and hands at hip height.
common_mistakes: Piking or kicking the feet back
Swinging the arms wide
Jumping far too high
safety: Use a speed rope and expect whipped shins while learning.
notes: Practise with single-double-single combinations.

name: Battle rope alternating waves
form_cues: Sit back in a half squat, chest up.
Drive one arm up as the other goes down, fast.
Keep the waves travelling all the way to the anchor.
common_mistakes: Standing up straight and using only arms
Waves dying halfway down the rope
safety: Anchor the rope securely and keep a neutral spine.
notes: Classic 20–30 sec on / 30–40 sec off.

name: Battle rope double waves
form_cues: Hold a half squat with a braced core.
Raise and lower both arms together.
Make big, even waves to the anchor.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back
Small, choppy waves
safety: Hinge at the hips rather than bending through the back.

name: Battle rope slams
form_cues: Raise both ropes overhead as you rise onto your toes.
Slam them down hard, dropping into a squat.
Reset quickly and repeat.
common_mistakes: Only using the arms with no leg drive
Rounding the back on the slam
safety: Keep your back neutral; don't overreach the arms behind the head.

name: Battle rope circles
form_cues: Make big circles with both arms, in sync.
Switch direction—inward, then outward.
Keep your stance athletic and core tight.
common_mistakes: Tiny circles from the wrists
Shrugging the shoulders
safety: Reduce range if you feel shoulder pinching.

name: Battle rope grappler throws
form_cues: Hold both rope ends together at one hip.
Pivot and swing them across to the other hip in an arc.
Drive the turn from your legs and hips.
common_mistakes: Twisting the lower back without pivoting the feet
Using only the arms
safety: Pivot your back foot to protect your knees and lower back.

name: Punching bag rounds
form_cues: Wrap your hands and stand at arm's length from the bag.
Throw combinations, then move around the bag.
Return your hands to your face after every punch.
common_mistakes: Pushing the bag instead of snapping punches
Hands dropping as you tire
Holding your breath
safety: Always wear wraps and gloves; build intensity gradually to protect wrists.
notes: Typical: 3 × 3 min rounds with 1 min rest.

name: Heavy bag jab-cross
form_cues: Snap the lead hand straight out, then back to the chin.
Pivot the back foot and turn the hip for the cross.
Keep the non-punching hand guarding your face.
common_mistakes: Winding up before punching
Not rotating the back foot on the cross
safety: Punch with the first two knuckles and a straight wrist.

name: Heavy bag hooks
form_cues: Bend the arm about 90° and keep the elbow up.
Turn the hips and pivot the lead foot into the punch.
Bring the hand straight back to guard.
common_mistakes: Swinging wide with an open arm
Punching with arm only, no hip turn
safety: Keep the wrist straight to avoid sprains.

name: Heavy bag uppercuts
form_cues: Dip slightly with the knees, then drive up.
Punch upward with the palm facing you.
Keep the other hand guarding your chin.
common_mistakes: Dropping the hand low before punching
Leaning back as you punch
safety: An uppercut bag or teardrop bag is best; go lighter on a straight hanging bag.

name: Heavy bag jab-cross-hook
form_cues: Jab, cross, then lead hook in one smooth flow.
Let the cross's hip turn load the hook.
Reset to stance with hands up after each combo.
common_mistakes: Pausing between punches
Dropping the rear hand during the hook
safety: Stay in range so you don't overreach and strain the shoulder.
notes: Count each full combination as one rep.

name: Heavy bag punch-outs
form_cues: Square up close to the bag.
Throw fast, straight punches non-stop.
Keep punches short and snappy, not wild.
common_mistakes: Wild, looping punches that hurt wrists
Leaning on the bag
safety: Use proper gloves and wraps; stop if a wrist or knuckle hurts.
notes: Great finisher: 20 sec all-out / 40 sec rest.

name: Heavy bag roundhouse kicks
form_cues: Step out, pivot on the standing foot, and turn the hip over.
Strike with the shin, not the foot.
Return quickly to a guarded stance.
common_mistakes: Kicking with the foot and hurting the instep
Leaning too far back
safety: Start light; shins need time to condition.

name: Heavy bag front kick
form_cues: Chamber the knee high before extending.
Push through the ball of the foot into the bag.
Keep your hands up and recover to stance.
common_mistakes: Kicking with toes and jamming them
Locking out the knee hard
safety: Strike with the ball of the foot, toes pulled back.

name: Heavy bag knees
form_cues: Grip the top of the bag as if clinching.
Pull the bag in as you drive the knee up and through.
Rise onto the toes of your standing foot.
common_mistakes: Kneeing with hips pushed back
Not alternating sides
safety: Keep a firm grip; a swinging bag can catch you off balance.

name: Kickboxing bag rounds
form_cues: Mix punches, kicks and knees in combinations.
Finish each combo with a step or angle change.
Pace yourself to last the full round.
common_mistakes: Throwing single strikes with no flow
Dropping the guard on kicks
safety: Wrap hands, warm up the hips, and start with light kicks.

name: Speed bag
form_cues: Set the bag at mouth or chin height.
Hit in a steady rhythm with small circular motions.
Let the bag rebound three times before the next hit.
common_mistakes: Hitting too hard and losing rhythm
Arms too far from the bag
safety: Wear light gloves or wraps to protect your knuckles.
notes: No speed-bag gear id exists; 'bag' (punching bag) is used as nearest. Mostly a timing and shoulder endurance drill.

name: Treadmill walk
form_cues: Walk tall in the middle of the belt.
Swing your arms; let go of the handrails.
Use a brisk pace, around 5–6 km/h.
common_mistakes: Holding the handrails the whole time
Walking too close to the front
safety: Clip on the safety key and straddle the belt before starting.

name: Incline treadmill walk
form_cues: Set an incline of 5–15% and a steady pace.
Stand upright and push through the whole foot.
Hands off the rails, arms swinging.
common_mistakes: Leaning back on the handrails
Cranking the incline so high you hunch
safety: Lower the incline if your lower back or Achilles feel strained.

name: 12-3-30 treadmill workout
form_cues: Set the incline to 12% and speed to about 5 km/h.
Walk for 30 minutes without holding the rails.
Keep your chest up and strides natural.
common_mistakes: Gripping the handrails
Jumping straight in without building up
safety: Build up from shorter durations or lower incline; stop if calves or shins ache.
notes: Popular viral protocol: 12% incline, 3 mph (~4.8 km/h), 30 minutes.

name: Treadmill run
form_cues: Set a 1% incline to mimic outdoor running.
Run in the middle of the belt with quick, light steps.
Look ahead, not down at the console.
common_mistakes: Holding the rails
Overstriding and landing far in front
safety: Use the safety key and step onto the side rails to stop.

name: Treadmill intervals
form_cues: Alternate fast running with easy jogging or walking.
Change speed with the buttons, not by jumping off.
Keep form tall and relaxed at speed.
common_mistakes: Straddling the belt on/off at high speed
Setting the sprint speed beyond control
safety: Use the safety key; build sprint speed gradually.
notes: Example: 1 min fast / 1–2 min easy × 8.

name: Stationary bike
form_cues: Set the saddle at hip height when standing beside it.
Keep a slight knee bend at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Pedal smoothly at 80–100 rpm.
common_mistakes: Saddle too low so knees ache
Bouncing on the saddle at high cadence
safety: Easy on knees and great for rehab—adjust the seat properly first.
notes: Log distance too if your bike shows it.

name: Recumbent bike
form_cues: Slide the seat so your knee is slightly bent at full reach.
Sit back against the backrest.
Push through the whole foot smoothly.
common_mistakes: Seat too close so knees come up high
Pedalling with no resistance
safety: Good option for back pain or balance issues since you're supported.
notes: No separate gear id; uses 'bike'.

name: Spin bike intervals
form_cues: Alternate seated sprints with standing climbs.
Add resistance rather than spinning out of control.
Keep hips steady and core engaged out of the saddle.
common_mistakes: Too little resistance so you bounce
Bobbing the upper body when standing
safety: Set up the bike properly and use clipped or caged pedals.

name: Tabata bike
equipment: Air bike, spin bike or stationary bike
form_cues: Sprint all-out for 20 seconds.
Pedal easy for 10 seconds.
Repeat 8 rounds without stopping.
common_mistakes: Pacing it like steady cardio
Skipping a proper warm-up
safety: Very intense—skip if you have heart or blood pressure concerns without medical clearance.
notes: Original Tabata protocol: 8 × 20 sec all-out / 10 sec rest. Warm up for 5–10 min first.

name: Air bike
form_cues: Push and pull the handles while you pedal.
Sit tall and keep a steady rhythm.
Remember: the harder you go, the harder it gets.
common_mistakes: Using only the legs
Starting too hard and blowing up
safety: Fan resistance rises fast—build up gradually.
notes: Can also log calories in notes.

name: Air bike intervals
form_cues: Sprint hard using arms and legs together.
Recover with slow, easy pedalling.
Keep each sprint the same quality.
common_mistakes: Going too hard on the first sprint
Hunching over the handles
safety: Extremely demanding—warm up well and stop if dizzy.
notes: Examples: 10 sec on / 50 sec off × 10, or 30/30.

name: Rowing machine
form_cues: Legs, hips, then arms on the drive.
Arms, hips, then legs on the return.
Keep the handle level and wrists flat.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms first
Rounding the back at the catch
Damper set to 10
safety: Keep a neutral spine; set the damper around 3–5.
notes: Roughly 60% legs, 20% hips/back, 20% arms.

name: Rowing intervals
form_cues: Row each piece at a hard, steady split.
Keep your stroke rate controlled (26–32).
Rest 1–2 min between pieces.
common_mistakes: Spiking the stroke rate and losing power
Collapsing posture when tired
safety: Keep a neutral back throughout; stop if your lower back aches.

name: 2,000 m row test
form_cues: Plan an even split and stick to it.
Settle into rhythm after a strong first 10 strokes.
Empty the tank in the last 250 m.
common_mistakes: Going out way too fast
Losing technique in the middle 1,000 m
safety: A maximal effort—only do it when fully warmed up and healthy.
notes: Benchmark test for rowing fitness; repeat every 6–8 weeks.

name: Elliptical
form_cues: Stand tall with your weight through the whole foot.
Push and pull the handles to involve the upper body.
Use resistance so you're not just gliding.
common_mistakes: Leaning on the handles
Zero resistance, high speed
safety: A low-impact choice for sore knees or hips.

name: Stair climber
form_cues: Stand tall and step through the whole foot.
Hold the rails lightly for balance only.
Pick a speed you can sustain without leaning.
common_mistakes: Hunching and leaning on the rails
Taking tiny steps on the toes
safety: Use the stop button rather than jumping off a moving machine.

name: Ski erg
form_cues: Reach tall, then drive the handles down by hinging hips.
Finish with hands past your hips.
Let the arms float back up as you stand tall.
common_mistakes: Squatting deep instead of hinging
Pulling with arms only
safety: Hinge with a neutral back; don't crunch your spine forward.

name: Curved treadmill run
form_cues: Move forward on the curve to speed up, back to slow down.
Run tall with quick, light steps.
Stay near the middle to hold a steady pace.
common_mistakes: Drifting too far forward and accelerating
Heavy heel-striking
safety: Use the handrails to get on and off safely; the belt keeps moving.

name: Curved treadmill sprints
form_cues: Lean into the curve and drive hard with your arms.
Stay on the balls of your feet.
Step back onto the rails to stop and rest.
common_mistakes: Sprinting cold without warm-up
Looking down at the belt
safety: Hold the rails when stepping off; the belt freewheels for a few seconds.
notes: Example: 8 × 20 sec all-out / 40 sec rest.

name: Arm bike
form_cues: Sit tall with the crank at shoulder height.
Pedal smoothly with your hands.
Switch direction halfway through.
common_mistakes: Hunching forward
Too much resistance so you jerk the cranks
safety: Useful when legs are injured; keep resistance low if shoulders are sore.
notes: No arm-ergometer gear id; 'bike' used as nearest.

name: VersaClimber
form_cues: Move opposite arm and leg together.
Use long, full strokes before speeding up.
Stay upright, close to the machine.
common_mistakes: Short, choppy strokes
Leaning back away from the machine
safety: Brutally intense; start with short intervals.
notes: No VersaClimber gear id; 'stairs' (stair climber) used as nearest.
